system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: A square, with a triangle attached to each side. Each triangle shares a side with the square, shown with a dotted line.]
The shape shown above is cut out of cardboard. The triangle flaps are then folded up along the dotted lines until they touch the edges of the flaps next to them.

Complete the diagram below to show what the shape would look like when viewed from directly above.

[Image: A square.]

Figure, described in words:
Top diagram: A flat net composed of a central square with dashed sides, each side joined to the base of an identical isosceles triangle pointing outward.
Bottom diagram: A square drawn with solid lines, representing the outer border of the shape viewed directly from above, awaiting completion.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw the outline of the square as the outer border (the base of the pyramid). Inside it, draw both diagonals, joining each corner to the opposite corner, so that they cross at the centre. The centre point is where the four folded flaps meet at the top (the apex), and the four lines from the centre to the corners are the edges where neighbouring flaps touch. So the completed diagram is a square with an X through its middle, the view a square pyramid gives from directly above.

llm_thinking: This is the classic TIMSS square pyramid folding question - when the triangular flaps fold up to meet at an apex, viewing the pyramid from directly above should show the square base with diagonal lines connecting to the center point where the apex sits.
